events.title: Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima
events.description: The United States dropped the atomic bomb 'Little Boy' on the Japanese city of Hiroshima from the B-29 bomber Enola Gay, killing an estimated 70,000 to 80,000 people instantly and tens of thousands more from injuries and radiation in the following months.
events.significance: This was the first use of a nuclear weapon in warfare. It hastened the end of World War II and ushered in the nuclear age, shaping global politics, arms control debates, and the Cold War.

events.title: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
events.description: Francis II abdicated as Holy Roman Emperor and dissolved the empire under pressure from Napoleon Bonaparte, after the creation of the Confederation of the Rhine. He continued to rule as Francis I of Austria.
events.significance: The act ended a political entity that had existed for roughly a thousand years and reshaped the political order of Central Europe, paving the way for later German unification.

events.title: Voting Rights Act Signed into Law
events.description: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act of 1965 in the President's Room of the U.S. Capitol, outlawing discriminatory voting practices such as literacy tests that had been used to disenfranchise Black Americans in the South.
events.significance: The law was a landmark achievement of the Civil Rights Movement and dramatically increased voter registration and political participation among African Americans.

events.title: First Website Made Publicly Available
events.description: British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee published the first website on the World Wide Web, hosted at CERN, providing information about the WWW project and how to use it.
events.significance: This opened the World Wide Web to the public and began the transformation of communication, commerce, and information access worldwide.

events.title: Birth of Alexander Fleming
events.description: Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming was born at Lochfield Farm in Ayrshire, Scotland. He later discovered penicillin in 1928, the first widely used antibiotic.
events.significance: Fleming's discovery revolutionized medicine, saved millions of lives, and earned him the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
